'''Arapaso''' ({{Langx|arj|Kõ'neá|links=no}}, Arapafo)<ref>{{Cite book |last=Silva |first=Alcionílio Brüzzi Alves da |url=http://www.etnolinguistica.org/biblio:silva-1962-civilizacao |title=A civilização indígena do Uaupés |date=1962 |website= |location=São Paulo |pages=96–97 |language=pt |access-date=2025-10-15}}</ref> is an extinct, poorly attesed eastern [[Tucanoan languages|Tucanoan language]] of [[Brazil]], closely related to [[Miriti language|Miriti]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.2 - Arapaso |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/arap1275 |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>

== Geographic distribution ==
Arapaso was spoken in the northwestern [[Amazonas (Brazilian state)|Amazonas State]] in the Upper [[Rio Negro (Amazon)|Río Negro]] region. Speakers were found in the [[Uaupés River|Vale de Uaupés]], within the [[Alto Rio Negro Indigenous Territory]] and the Terra Indígena Médio Rio Negro II.<ref name="Moseley2008"/>

== Status ==
Arapaso is sometimes considered to be an extinct dialect of the [[Tucano language|Tukano language]] (the ethnic population was reported as 328 in 2001). All members of the ethnic group were bilingual in Tukano, and the community was undergoing a [[language shift]] to it. Younger generations have also received schooling in [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]].<ref name="Moseley2008">{{cite book |last=Moseley |first=Christopher |title=Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages |publisher=Routledge |date=2008-03-10 |isbn=978-1-135-79640-2 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p-7ON7Rvx_AC&pg=PT161 |access-date=2025-10-19 |page=}}</ref>
